A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same decentralized-learning study despite the changed title. Their main text, figures, table, equations, and appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-classification experiments, communication-window studies, and optimizer, topology, initialization, and heterogeneity analyses in Figures 1, 3, and C.1–C.3.

after.justification: V2 reports original classification experiments and communication analyses in Figures 1–2 and C.1–C.5, including SGD and AdamW comparisons.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, local optimization followed by gossip averaging, and final global parameter averaging are retained. Both SGD and AdamW already appeared in v1. V2's discussion of adaptive communication and gossip-based approximation does not introduce an implemented method component.

E1.justification: Both retain image-classification experiments on CIFAR-100 and Tiny ImageNet and list CIFAR-10 in Appendix C.1. The heterogeneity and communication-topology scenarios already appear in v1. Additional optimizer and agent-count configurations do not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain periodically synchronized server-based/federated training and fully local training followed by final merging. FedAvg/FedAdamW and their one-shot labels clarify these existing roles. D-PSGD and periodic global averaging are discussed as prior work, without new empirical baseline comparisons.

E3.justification: The headline Figure 1 comparisons shift from 16-agent AdamW to 32-agent SGD, with peer communication probability 0.2. V2 also reports 32-agent AdamW comparisons. Retained 16-agent curves are now captioned with probability 0.2 rather than one peer every round, and Appendix C.1 changes pretrained ResNet's AdamW learning rate from 1e-3 to 5e-4. These are reported setting changes; reused curves do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: V2 extends optimizer and agent-count consistency checks through 32-agent SGD and AdamW comparisons for both architectures. Most existing analyses are retained: communication windows, no-communication controls, peer frequency, topology, initialization, batch size, learning rate, and heterogeneity. V1 Figures C.1b–c and C.2–C.3 largely reappear as v2 Figures C.3–C.5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The plotted counterfactual-model curves are not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V1 Figure 1's accuracy curves reappear in v2 Figure C.1, while v2 Figure 1 reports new 32-agent SGD results and Figure C.2 adds 32-agent AdamW results. The new SGD ResNet comparison reaches approximately 48% after merging versus 56% for FedAvg. V1's 16-agent SGD panel in Figure C.1a is no longer reported. This substantially revises the headline evidence under different conditions, without establishing a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Theorem 1/D.7 replaces the signed ε^-2 sum A(t) contribution with ε^-1 sqrt([sum A(t)]+), explicitly requires shared initialization, and rewrites the step-size/rate derivation. Corollary D.2 changes the noise bound's dependence on p; Proposition 3 uses uniformly bounded gradients instead of slowly varying gradients. V2 also adds the zero-gap/noise discussion in Remark D.1 and restricts mergeability weights to [0,1].

C1.justification: V1's headline claims of recovering server-based performance and outperforming centralized mini-batch SGD become significant improvement or performance close to federated learning, and matching parallel SGD's convergence rate. These narrow central empirical and theoretical claims. The late-communication and persistent-mergeability claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of mergeability without consensus and a high-loss ring surrounding a low-loss basin, discusses communication costs and gossip approximation, and develops model-merging and adaptive-communication implications in Section 6. V1's explicit surge-and-decline explanation is removed. The vision-only limitation is retained after relocation.

D1.justification: Appendices A/C.1 add optimizer-specific tuning ranges and SGD learning rates, plus the hexadecagon/Wachspress construction, test-set loss evaluation, and notebook reference for Figure 1c. Existing hardware, runtime, and preprocessing details largely remain. The warning about overlapping samples across agents is removed; the study's own code remains promised rather than supplied.

R1.justification: V2 expands comparisons with federated learning and gossip, explicitly credits Lian et al. (2017) with prior final global merging, and positions novelty around systematically studying its non-IID benefits. Added references include McMahan et al. (2017), Jelasity et al. (2005), Chen et al. (2025), and Crisostomi et al. (2024). Much of the existing model-merging review simply moves to Appendix B.3.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the introduction, contribution narrative, related-work discussion, and theoretical explanations. It moves evaluation metrics into the preliminaries, adds Appendix C.2, relocates the model-merging review, replaces the conclusion with implications and discussions, and adds publication statements. These constitute extensive narrative and structural revision.

P2.justification: V2 combines the training-scheme illustration with the main results into a four-panel Figure 1, redraws the schematic, and adds a merging inset. Appendix plots are regrouped and expanded, with the former main accuracy curves moved to Figure C.1. The document also adopts different title, heading, header, and citation layouts; many retained plots preserve their underlying curves.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's stronger recovery and acceleration framing, v2 offers better calibrated claims, clearer prior-work attribution, and reproducible visualization details. Appendix D also explicitly handles the sign of cumulative A(t). These gains are partly offset by inconsistencies: Section 5.2's prose disagrees with the displayed rate's ε dependence, the new CLIP AdamW tuning grid excludes the selected 1e-5 learning rate, and the sample-overlap warning is removed. The net improvement is limited.
